guard_streams.write_limit: OMR and Public Review classifications, maps and planned-build submissions are subsidy-targeting evidence; postcodes are presentational and cannot prove current parcel coverage or orderability.

facts.detail: The Buckinghamshire, Hertfordshire and East Berkshire public-review RFI was updated on 23 June 2026.
The document cites £5 billion for the hardest-to-reach parts of the UK.
The preceding OMR ran from 12 August to 13 September 2021.
The OMR requested current and planned broadband investment over the next three years and beyond where available.
The Public Review aims to validate OMR outcomes and BDUK mapping.
The review invited feedback from the public, businesses, ISPs and infrastructure operators.
The document states subsidy will only be used for premises designated White.
Postcodes are used for presentation only and do not determine intervention areas for subsidy.
A White and Under Review UPRN list can be supplied subject to relevant data-sharing arrangements.
The process sequence is OMR, Public Review, intervention-area determination and procurement.

guard_streams.write_limit: Historic OMR/Public Review classifications and redesigned procurement scope are subsidy-planning evidence; they do not verify present-day serviceability or measured speed for selected parcels.

facts.detail: The Norfolk Lot 7 closure notice was updated on 23 June 2026.
The notice concerns procurement to extend gigabit-capable broadband across Norfolk.
The preceding Norfolk OMR ran from March to April 2021.
The Norfolk Public Review ran from 19 August to 20 September 2021.
BDUK states that only White premises are subsidy targets.
Under Review premises require further review before release for build.
The postcode-level map is presentational and does not identify which UPRNs are White or Under Review.
The closure notice reports 94,136 White premises.
A May 2026 redesign revised the contract to around 33,000 premises backed by £61.9 million.
The notice states national rolling OMR returns are collected in January, May and September.
